papers.title_en: Are Single-Leader-Multi-Follower Problems Particular Cases of Bilevel Optimization?
papers.authors: Didier Aussel, David Salas, Martin Schmidt
papers.evidence: 将SLMF问题重新表述为双层优化
papers.tldr: 本文挑战了单领袖多跟随者（SLMF）问题比双层优化更难的传统观念，研究了将SLMF问题重构为等价双层优化问题的可行性。研究发现乐观SLMF可转化为等价双层优化，而悲观SLMF则与三层优化问题等价，揭示了多跟随者在乐观与悲观方法之间意想不到的复杂度鸿沟。
papers.abstract_en: For more than 20 years, single-leader multi-follower (SLMF) problems have been treated as a more difficult class of problems in comparison to bilevel optimization. In this work we challenge this common belief, studying whether SLMF problems can be reformulated as equivalent bilevel optimization problems. We consider both optimistic and pessimistic formulations. For the optimistic case the answer is positive: We derive an equivalent bilevel problem by representing the followers' equilibria as fixed points of the solution mapping of a single optimization problem. For pessimistic problems, the situation is different. We show that every optimistic trilevel problem admits an equivalent pessimistic SLMF formulation with two followers. Conversely, for every pessimistic SLMF problem verifying a mild attainability assumption we establish an equivalent optimistic trilevel reformulation. The reformulations are easy, readily tractable, and they preserve convex and linear data. Thus, unless $\text{NP}=Σ_2^p$, we deduce as byproduct that multiple followers induce an unexpected complexity gap between optimistic and pessimistic approaches, which is not the case when considering one follower alone.

papers.title_en: FedRAPP: Federated Test-Time Prompt Tuning for Vision-Language Models with Reliability-Aware Prompt Personalization
papers.authors: Syed Md. Ahnaf Hasan, Md Akil Raihan Iftee, Sajib Mistry, Amin Ahsan Ali, AKM Mahbubur Rahman
papers.tldr: 本文针对无源联邦测试时提示词微调（SF-FTTPT）场景，研究了视觉-语言模型在异构未标记测试流下的协同适应问题。针对传统聚合方法在非IID分布下面临的提示词漂移和特异化难题，提出了FedRAPP框架，通过可靠性评估、动量提示词记忆和相似度引导的同伴聚合，实现鲁棒的个性化适应，在多个基准数据集上显著优于现有基线。
papers.abstract_en: Federated prompt learning enables vision-language models like CLIP to collaboratively adapt lightweight soft prompts across distributed clients without sharing raw data. However, existing federated prompt learning methods are designed primarily for supervised settings with labeled client data and assumed relatively stable training distributions. At test time, source-free federated prompt tuning remains largely unexplored. Clients may receive unlabeled target samples with heterogeneous, often non-IID distributions that differ substantially across clients and from the source training distribution, causing locally adapted prompts to drift in different directions and reducing the effectiveness of federated aggregation. In this work, we explore Source-Free Federated Test-Time Prompt Tuning (SF-FTTPT), where distributed clients collaboratively adapt soft prompts on unlabeled test streams without access to source data. Our study reveals that conventional federated aggregation methods struggle under heterogeneous client distributions, as locally adapted prompts become increasingly specialized and difficult to combine effectively. To address this challenge, we propose FedRAPP, a personalized aggregation framework that combines reliability-aware client assessment, server-side exponential moving-average prompt memory, and similarity-guided peer aggregation. FedRAPP selectively incorporates information from reliable and compatible clients while preserving local specialization, enabling more robust adaptation under distribution shift. Extensive experiments across nine CLIP benchmark datasets and ImageNet variants demonstrate that FedRAPP consistently outperforms standard federated aggregation baselines under heterogeneous client distributions while maintaining the efficiency advantages of prompt-only adaptation.

papers.title_en: Knowledge-Guided Distributional Prompt Learning with Visual Hierarchy for Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection
papers.authors: Jiyul Ham, Seongho Yoon, Yonggon Jung, Sangjae Lee, Jun-Geol Baek
papers.evidence: 用于零样本检测的分布提示学习
papers.tldr: 该论文针对零样本异常检测中未充分利用正常与异常关联及细粒度定位的问题，提出了一种名为HiDist的知识引导层级分布提示学习框架。通过以正常参考建模异常分布、结合蒙特卡洛采样生成提示变体，并将其特化为全局与局部表示，HiDist有效提升了图像级检测与像素级定位性能，在工业和医疗数据集上展现出优异的跨数据集泛化能力。
papers.abstract_en: Zero-shot anomaly detection (ZSAD) aims to detect anomalies in previously unseen classes using auxiliary images, with applications such as industrial visual inspection and medical imaging. Recent vision-language-model-based approaches improve ZSAD by aligning textual and visual representations, while distributional prompting further models prompt variability for unseen categories. However, existing methods do not explicitly combine normality-referenced distributional modeling with hierarchy-specific prompt specialization, limiting their ability to model anomalous semantics relative to normality while addressing both image-level detection and fine-grained localization. We propose Hierarchical Knowledge-Guided Distributional Prompt Learning (HiDist), a normality-referenced hierarchical distributional prompt framework for ZSAD. HiDist models each prompt token with a diagonal Gaussian distribution and generates stochastic prompt variations through Monte Carlo sampling. Rather than learning normal and anomalous distributions independently, anomalous prompt distributions are parameterized as deviations from learned normal references, explicitly encoding their dependency. The resulting distributions are specialized into global and local representations for image-level detection and pixel-level localization, respectively, while an adapted global visual representation guides hierarchical alignment. Experiments on seven industrial and medical datasets demonstrate strong cross-dataset performance across anomaly detection and localization tasks. Extensive ablation and representation analyses further support the effectiveness of the proposed distributional modeling and hierarchy-specific representation learning.

papers.title_en: ProactGen: Learning Proactive Clarification for Video Generation
papers.authors: Zhixiao Wang, Yang Chen, Yifan Xu, Chenbin Li, Yue Chang, Kai Long, Fengming Dong, Limin Wang
papers.tldr: 针对现有视频生成由于提示词模糊而需要反复迭代且耗时高的问题，本文提出了ProactGen框架。该方法通过强化学习训练视觉语言模型，根据初始提示词和低成本生成的视频草稿主动向用户提出澄清问题，从而高效引导生成符合真实意图的高质量视频。
papers.abstract_en: Recent advances in video generation let users create high-quality videos from natural language descriptions, yet obtaining results that match user intent remains time-consuming: individual generations are computationally expensive, and underspecified prompts force repeated cycles of generation, inspection, and revision. Existing video prompt optimization methods improve generation through automatic rewriting, but cannot supply the ideas and preferences that were not in the initial description. We propose ProactGen, a video generation framework that learns proactive clarification, eliciting user intent through questions grounded in generated video drafts. Specifically, we train a vision-language model as a questioning policy with reinforcement learning: observing the initial prompt and a video draft, it learns to ask the questions most valuable to downstream generation, rewarded by the alignment between the final generated video and a target reference. We further find that effective questioning does not require drafts of final-output quality, and exploit this property by generating drafts with fewer denoising steps, keeping the added cost of clarification low. Experiments show that ProactGen improves target alignment over direct generation by at least 1.8x the gain of the strongest baselines. Moreover, a single round of ProactGen already exceeds the alignment that the strongest baseline reaches after four refinement rounds, in 29% of its time.

papers.title_en: ShadowFPT: Backdooring Federated Prompt Tuning via Shadow Triggers
papers.authors: Kun Zhai, Teng Li, Yunhao Feng, Xingjun Ma
papers.evidence: 联邦提示微调中的安全风险
papers.tldr: 本文针对联邦提示微调（FPT）提出了一种名为ShadowFPT的隐蔽后门攻击方法。由于FPT冻结了预训练大模型的骨干网络，恶意客户端可通过表示空间操纵后门行为，而无需修改骨干网络。实验表明，该方法在保持正常精度的同时，显著提升了攻击成功率。
papers.abstract_en: Federated Prompt Tuning (FPT) adapts large vision--language models by freezing the pretrained backbone and optimizing only lightweight prompt parameters across clients. Although this design improves communication and parameter efficiency, it creates an overlooked security risk. Since the backbone is shared and frozen, a malicious client can induce backdoor behavior through the representation space while keeping its uploaded prompt updates close to benign ones. We propose \textbf{ShadowFPT}, a targeted backdoor attack that exploits this frozen-backbone attack surface. ShadowFPT first pretrains a learnable \emph{Shadow Trigger} against the frozen CLIP visual encoder, using either auxiliary public data or the malicious client's local data, so that triggered inputs are steered toward the target class in representation space. During federated prompt tuning, the malicious client adapts the trigger under the current global prompt and then optimizes its local prompt on both clean and triggered samples. Only prompt parameters are uploaded to the server, while the trigger and frozen encoders remain local. By shifting most of the attack burden from prompt updates to trigger-induced representation steering, ShadowFPT achieves targeted misclassification while preserving prompt-space stealthiness. Across multiple datasets, aggregation rules, and non-IID federated partitions, ShadowFPT increases the attack success rate from 19.81\% to 90.36\% in our main setting, while maintaining clean accuracy. It remains effective across textual, visual, and joint vision--language prompt tuning. These results identify frozen backbones as stealthy and underexplored backdoor surfaces in federated prompt tuning, suggesting that defenses based only on prompt-update anomaly detection are insufficient.

papers.title_en: Language Models Learn to Improve Language Models
papers.authors: Minhua Lin, Zijun Wang, Zewen Liu, Zhaotian Weng, Bing He, Zhan Shi, Benoit Dumoulin, Xiang Zhang, Suhang Wang, Hanqing Lu
papers.evidence: 自动化语言模型开发与改进建议优化
papers.tldr: 本文探讨了利用大语言模型（LLMs）实现递归自我改进以自动化AI研究的潜力。针对真实反馈成本高昂以及代理反馈在策略偏移时不可靠的挑战，作者提出了LM2LM框架。该方法通过强化学习训练LLM生成有效的语言模型改进提案，利用研究世界模型（RWM）提供可扩展的奖励反馈，并定期通过真实执行来维护反馈的可靠性。在多个开发环境中的评估表明，LM2LM能够使较小模型超越更强大的模型基线，同时降低数据生成成本，并具备良好的泛化能力。
papers.abstract_en: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to automate AI research, including language-model (LM) development, offering a potential path toward recursive self-improvement. However, turning experimental feedback into a learned ability to propose effective improvements across models faces two challenges. First, training such an ability with real feedback is expensive: reinforcement learning (RL) requires evaluating tens of thousands of proposals, each potentially requiring a full model-training run. Even at ten GPU-hours per run, reward collection alone would consume hundreds of thousands of GPU-hours, motivating a cheaper surrogate. Second, surrogate feedback can become unreliable as policy optimization favors overestimated proposals when the proposal distribution shifts. To address these challenges, we propose LM2LM, which trains LLMs with RL to generate effective LM improvement proposals. To provide scalable feedback, we use a research world model (RWM), a frozen LLM that predicts proposal gains from real experimental records provided in context, as the reward model for RL. To maintain feedback reliability, we periodically execute current-policy proposals ranked highly by the RWM and add their measured outcomes to its context. Across eight autoregressive and diffusion LM development environments, real-execution evaluations on held-out tasks show that LM2LM enables Qwen3.8-27B to outperform GPT-6-sol, even when GPT-6-sol is given 300 real experimental records in context, while requiring 33% lower data-generation cost. LM2LM also generalizes to a model family unseen during training.

papers.title_en: VISTA: Steering LLMs with Latent User Values Inferred from a Few Survey Answers
papers.authors: Yinuo Xu, Jadie Adams, Brian Hu, Shivani Kumar, David Jurgens, Arslan Basharat
papers.evidence: 无需增加提示词Token的引导干预
papers.tldr: 本文介绍了VISTA（Value-Informed Steering and Targeted Acquisition）框架，通过少量问卷回答推断用户的潜在价值观，并利用超网络对冻结的LLM进行用户特定的干预。该方法无需增加提示词长度，即可实现精准的用户个性化对齐，显著降低了问卷认知负担并保持了高准确率，为多元化对齐提供了低成本的可行方案。
papers.abstract_en: Personalizing a language model requires knowing what a person values, which stays largely consistent across tasks. Yet most methods either learn task-specific preferences or place the user's profile in the prompt, where models struggle to act on it. We introduce VISTA (Value-Informed Steering and Targeted Acquisition), which infers a latent profile from users' (full or partial) survey answers, and maps the profile through a hypernetwork to a user-specific steering intervention in a frozen LLM to select answer choices or generate free-text responses. Given the same evidence, VISTA matches or beats in-context profiles on synthetic preferences (Food2D), the World Values Survey (WVS), and PrimeX, without adding prompt tokens. To reduce the cognitive burden of completing full surveys, VISTA also chooses which questions to ask and when to stop: on WVS it stops after 6% of the questionnaire while retaining 94% of the full-history gain, where standard adaptive testing retains at most 42%. The dominant steering direction is an interpretable value axis on which VISTA places unseen users accurately. Our results point toward pluralistic alignment that adapts to individuals at deployable cost.

papers.title_en: GLOBE: Evolving Structured Agentic Memory for E-commerce Product Optimization in Generative Search
papers.authors: Hyunseo Kim, Suil Choe, Sukkyoung So, Daeyeon Yi
papers.evidence: 用于优化的演化提示策略
papers.tldr: 本文针对生成式搜索中的电商商品优化问题，提出了一种名为GLOBE的智能体框架。该框架通过演进式的结构化代理记忆，将优化知识存储在不断更新的显式字段行为手册中，实现了语言代理的持续自我改进与泛化能力。
papers.abstract_en: Optimizing product listings for generative search requires language agents not only to rewrite effectively but also to continually self-improve by retaining successful strategies across diverse categories. However, existing approaches often treat structured listings as free-form text, leaving effective strategies implicit in prompts, search trajectories, or rewritten outputs rather than accumulating them as a reusable agentic memory. To address this limitation, we introduce GLOBE, an agentic framework that drives continual self-improvement by storing optimization knowledge in an evolving handbook of explicit, field-scoped behaviors. In each episode, an Editor applies relevant behaviors and receives rank-based feedback, which a Reflector converts into behavior updates. Crucially for dependable execution in real-world settings, a Moderator removes redundant proposals, a Curator commits accepted changes, and consistently harmful behaviors are deactivated. This cycle transforms episodic feedback into a persistent, field-scoped optimization memory. Experiments show that structured behaviors outperform monolithic prompt optimization, while feedback-driven evolution and moderation further improve effectiveness and reduce downside risk. The learned behaviors also remain effective on unseen product categories, suggesting that agentic memory evolution supports interpretable and transferable product optimization.
